subject: FastCommerce checkout tails — queue hold & temporary capacity request
messages:
From: Zara Yang <zara.yang@fastcommerce.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 10-20s tail spikes impacting checkout (urgent)

Monica —

We started seeing intermittent long-tail latency at checkout this morning around 07:40 PDT. P95 is fine but p99.9 jumps to 10–20s for a small fraction of requests (~0.6–1.2% of traffic) and we are seeing an associated increase in 5xx (mostly 503) during those spikes. Impact: a handful of customers report failed checkouts and abandoned carts.

Attached is a CSV with a few sample request IDs and timestamps. Our infra team noticed these correspond to the same model route and cluster. We are on Redwood Dedicated in us-west and currently using the default concurrency caps configured for our Dedicated pool.

Can you loop in ops and advise on immediate mitigations? This is customer-impacting and we may need executive attention if this continues.

Thanks,
Zara Yang
Head of Infrastructure, FastCommerce
---
Attachments: sample_request_ids_20290403.csv (text/csv)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Zara Yang <zara.yang@fastcommerce.com>, Jake Morris <jake.morris@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 10-20s tail spikes impacting checkout (urgent)

Zara —

Thanks for the heads up and for the sample IDs. We're prioritizing this. Quick summary of immediate next steps we plan to take (pending your permission for a short maintenance window or capacity bump):

- We will temporarily lift the per-instance concurrency cap on your Dedicated pool for the next 30 minutes to see if backpressure alleviates the tail.
- We'll enable an emergency drain on a small subset of nodes to flush any hot KV-cache state and restart the actor process if needed.
- Our oncall will collect a targeted heap of traces and the KV-key heatmap for the affected route. Please confirm a 20–30 minute window where we can do the bump; this should not require redirecting traffic but will increase node utilization.

Marissa / Vivek: can you validate whether a short concurrency bump is safe for FC-4782 (do we have headroom in the Dedicated pool)? Also please prepare a short exec-facing summary in case FastCommerce wants to escalate.

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Referenced attachments: sample_request_ids_20290403.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 10-20s tail spikes impacting checkout (urgent)

Monica —

Preliminary check on Dedicated pool FC-4782: we have ~18% spare GPU capacity across the pool right now. Short answer: we can do a temporary concurrency increase by +50% on the affected route for up to 45 minutes without breaching SLA on other tenants. However, here's what I'm seeing in telemetry that matters:

- The p99.9 spikes line up with a small set of hot keys in the KV cache for the personalization model. When a node hits its concurrency cap, requests queue and the runtime cannot refill the KV cache quickly — the combo produces long tail latencies.
- There are signs of prefix-cache miss storms when sessions with large context lengths are routed to the same GPU. That increases token processing time and triggers queueing at the runtime layer.

Immediate playbook (short-term):
1) Increase per-instance concurrency cap for route "fc-checkout-personalization" from 8 -> 12 for 30 minutes.
2) Temporarily enable prefix-prefetch policy for that route (reduce miss cost).
3) Rotate 2 warm nodes out to drain and restart the actor to flush hot key skew.

I've attached a tar of the discovered hotkeys and a time-series snapshot. Planning to run these changes at 09:30 PDT if Monica/Zara approve.

Marissa
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
---
Attachments: kvcache_hotkeys_20290403.tar.gz, latency_time_series_20290403.png

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Zara Yang <zara.yang@fastcommerce.com>, Jake Morris <jake.morris@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent 10-20s tail spikes impacting checkout (urgent)

Zara —

Thank you — please go ahead with the temporary capacity bump and rotate plan at 09:30 PDT. We'll execute the change and monitor for 30–45 minutes. Our SRE will keep a live thread and share telemetry; if we don't see improvement we'll escalate to a cross-functional exec sync.

Post-action summary (if helpful for your execs):
- Root cause hypothesis: KV-cache hot-key concentration + prefix-cache miss storms causing request queuing under concurrency cap.
- Immediate mitigations: concurrency bump, prefix prefetch, drain/restart small subset of warm nodes.
- Next steps (24–72h): add targeted kvcache sharding for hot keys, adjust routing policy to fan out long-context sessions, consider per-customer soft-concurrency guard to prevent single-customer bursts from impacting co-tenants.

I'll send a short exec note after the run.

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Zara Yang <zara.yang@fastcommerce.com>, Jake Morris <jake.morris@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: FastCommerce — post-mitigation exec summary and proposed follow-ups

Zara / Jake —

Quick executive summary after the 09:30 PDT mitigation window and follow-up observability run:

- Outcome: p99.9 tail deficit reduced from ~12–18s down to <1.2s for the monitored window; 5xx rates returned to baseline. We observed a reduction in queued requests on nodes where the concurrency cap was temporarily increased.
- What we did: temporary per-instance concurrency cap increase (8->12) for route fc-checkout-personalization, enabled prefix-prefetch for the route, drained and restarted 2 warm nodes to rebalance KV cache heat.
- Immediate risk: temporary bump means higher single-node utilization; we monitored memory and GPU temp and saw no failure conditions.

Recommended next steps (owners and ETA):
- SRE (Marissa): implement targeted kvcache sharding for known hot keys; ETA 72h.
- Runtime (Vivek): evaluate adaptive soft-concurrency per-customer to limit burst-induced queuing; ETA 5 working days for a small canary.
- Account team (Monica): coordinate a short follow-up exec readout with FastCommerce to review permanent mitigations and possible Dedicated pool scaling options; propose a 30-min call next week.

We attached the run telemetry and hotkey dump. Let me know any additional asks and if you'd like us to set up a short exec call early next week.

Thanks again for the quick signal — we’ll stay on monitoring for the next 48 hours and will proactively surface any regressions.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
